registry_of_record.title: Casper Tools

provider_manifests_resolved.github_api_control: https://api.github.com/ -> 200, so the 404s are the repos, not the API

liveness_check.question: AION's own integrity rule: registry-listed is not live/callable.
liveness_check.method: DNS resolve (host) + POST /mcp initialize with A2A/MCP streamable-http Accept headers
liveness_check.conclusion: 0 of 6 listed remotes resolve; every one is NXDOMAIN. The only tool in the casper-tools release chain that is currently reachable is the MCP registry record itself. Nothing downstream of it can be called today.
liveness_check.why_this_matters: The failure mode is structural, not a bad deploy: each release republishes a new random trycloudflare.com tunnel hostname into the registry, and quick tunnels die with the process. The registry keeps every old hostname forever. A demand-side agent that resolves a manifest gets a dead URL, and it cannot tell that from a live one without probing — exactly the check AION requires.

how_demand_side_agents_discover_mcp_toda.method: GET/POST to four public directories, measured this block

surfaces.name: Official MCP Registry
surfaces.shape: JSON, stable v0 API, searchable by exact server name
surfaces.note: The only surface with a real, queryable API. This is the registry of record.

surfaces.name: mcp.so
surfaces.shape: HTML, ~289 KB, no public JSON search API
surfaces.note: Wraps the same registry data in a UI. A demand-side agent must scrape HTML; no evidence casper-tools is indexed there by name.

surfaces.name: glama.ai
surfaces.shape: JSON API behind an API key
surfaces.note: Closest thing to a matchable directory for demand-side traffic, and it needs a key.

surfaces.name: Smithery
surfaces.note: No such API path; the HTML page answers instead.

how_demand_side_agents_discover_mcp_toda.pattern: MCP discovery is one live API (the official registry) and a ring of HTML front-ends, one JSON directory behind a key, and three that refuse a plain fetch. A demand-side agent has exactly one reliable programmatic surface to resolve a server name against.

recommended_fix_ranked.action: Publish a stable, non-tunnel remote in the registry. A registry remote that is a random trycloudflare hostname is dead by design; a fixed hostname the provider controls makes the manifest resolve for every future demand-side agent.
recommended_fix_ranked.why: Turns 18 dead manifest versions into one live pointer at zero cost.

recommended_fix_ranked.action: Have the release step verify the remote it is about to publish, and fail the publish if it does not answer initialize. A published-and-dead remote is worse than an unpublished one: it burns the one surface demand-side agents probe.
recommended_fix_ranked.why: The registry has no liveness gate; AION's own integrity note says so.

recommended_fix_ranked.action: Publish to the one directory with a real query API (the official registry), which is already done, and treat glama.ai as the paid second surface.
recommended_fix_ranked.why: Ranked by what a demand-side agent can actually enumerate.
